assets.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Revise the Dispatch conversation screen into a Slack-style shared channel experience. Image 1 is the user's Slack screenshot: use ONLY its visual hierarchy, dense readable all-left-aligned message rows, channel header, left conversation navigation, and right reply-thread panel. Do not reproduce its content, names, workspaces, menu bar, Slack logo, purple theme, or instructional text. Image 2 is the approved Dispatch screen: preserve its Dispatch icon, navy #1D3D6A rail, light gray-blue sidebar, white surfaces, aqua #4DD5CF selection accents, Inter typography and overall branded visual family. This is a new proposed screen, not an implementation screenshot.
Create a sharp, high fidelity, 16:10 desktop product screenshot. No device frame, perspective, decorative board, or headline outside the app.
Layout: slim navy icon rail at far left, 250px light sidebar, broad center discussion, 340px white right thread panel separated by a thin border. Sidebar: header Conversations; navy New conversation button; Find a conversation search; New project action; expanded project Dispatch Web with lock-marked conversations shared-conversations selected, agent-library, and passkey-sign-in. Another collapsed project Weekend plans; a Without a project group below. Archived conversations at bottom. No top app-wide toolbar, browser chrome, duplicate logo, notification counts, multiple workspace switcher or new Channels product destination.
Center: one compact header with lock icon, title Shared conversations, small project label Dispatch Web beneath, a members/avatar button labeled 4 participants, and a subtle ellipsis. No main tab strip because only one conversation is open. Below header the message history occupies the full main column. EVERY message including Chris is left aligned. No speech bubbles, no right-aligned human messages, no cards around ordinary messages. Use 32px avatars at a fixed left gutter, bold author names, muted small timestamps on same baseline, and concise body copy beneath. Consecutive messages from one author compact naturally.
At top a thin Today date divider. Then exactly this public conversation:
Chris · 5:42 PM: “Let's make this feel like a shared workspace. Everyone should be able to follow the discussion.”
Designer with small Agent badge · 5:43 PM: “A channel-style layout gives people and agents equal footing. Keep replies beside the main discussion.”
Under Designer's message a small avatar stack and blue text “2 replies”.
Developer with small Agent badge · 5:44 PM: “I'll bring Reviewer in before we settle the interaction details.”
A quiet indented system event: “Developer added Reviewer”.
Reviewer with small Agent badge · 5:45 PM: “I've read the conversation so far. @Developer, let's keep the participant list one click away.”
Developer with Agent badge · 5:46 PM: “Agreed. The conversation stays focused; details open on the right.”
A small per-message hover action strip appears near Designer's message with Reply and Copy icons only, not a row of emoji reactions. Do not invent reactions, calls, file tabs, huddles, canvases or workflow dashboards.
Right panel header Thread with close X. Repeat Designer's parent message compactly, then a thin line labeled 2 replies. Two all-left-aligned responses: Chris at 5:44 PM says “Yes—this is the direction.”; Reviewer with Agent badge at 5:46 PM says “Keep names visible and let a new participant catch up on the whole conversation.” A small independent Reply… composer sits below the thread messages, with formatting icons and navy send arrow. The main composer is pinned at the bottom of the center column: two rows, subtle formatting toolbar B I link list code, placeholder Message everyone…, lower toolbar @ and a navy Send button. Show no auto-cross-post checkbox; thread semantics remain a design proposal.
Bottom app bar only quiet Connected status and Dispatch / Chris. Lots of usable transcript width, restrained spacing like Slack, dark readable text. Keep the high-quality established Dispatch UI, not generic rounded chatbot cards. All specified labels spelled correctly.
assets.refinement: Refine this Dispatch shared-conversation design with one focused identity change. Keep the entire Slack-style screen layout, all-left-aligned message rows, exact text, typography, spacing, right Thread panel, composers, sidebar, colors, and selected conversation unchanged. Replace ALL photographic avatars, including the small participant stack and thread reply stack, with clear consistent designed identity icons. Chris is a navy circular avatar with the white letter C. Developer is a pale aqua circular avatar with a navy code-brackets icon. Designer is a pale aqua circular avatar with a navy palette icon. Reviewer is a pale aqua circular avatar with a navy magnifying-glass icon. Use the correct same icon for each author everywhere. Keep the small Agent badge on Developer, Designer and Reviewer. Chris is human: no Agent badge. Avoid faces or invented profile photos. Preserve the high-quality light Dispatch navy/aqua UI and every other part of the image.

assets.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Adapt the attached approved Dispatch desktop workspace into the New conversation creation state. Preserve the exact visual family: navy left rail, light project sidebar, white content, pale Details column, Inter, #1D3D6A navy, #4DD5CF aqua, thin gray-blue borders and calm spacing. Landscape 16:10, high fidelity crisp product screenshot, no device frame or presentation border.
The project Dispatch Web is selected in the grouped sidebar. Behind a light dimming scrim is its project page with the heading Dispatch Web and a New conversation button. Center an elegant approximately 600 px wide modal with white background and restrained shadow. The modal is the clearly legible focal point.
Modal heading New conversation and close X. Under it a small context line Project: Dispatch Web. Supporting sentence: “Choose agents to start with. You can add people and agents later.” A full-width search input says Find an agent. Below it exactly four clean list rows, each with a small avatar, agent name, one short description, and an accessible square checkbox on the right:
Dispatch — General assistance — unchecked.
Developer — Code and implementation — checked.
Designer — Product and interface design — checked.
Reviewer — Review and critique — unchecked.
Selected rows have a very pale aqua fill and dark navy checkmark; retain readable dark text. Developer and Designer are selected together. Do not show arbitrary instance IDs. Keep reusable definition selection understandable without teaching runtime internals. Do not add model selection, role permissions, a required conversation name, project creation fields, invitations by email, or a workflow wizard.
At the foot of the modal, show “2 agents selected” above or beside a persistent action row with Cancel and a navy Start conversation button. All content and buttons visible without clipping. The existing shell remains recognizable beneath the overlay. This is a proposed visual design, with illustrative available agents. Render all specified labels accurately.

High fidelity landscape product screen, sharp legible text, no device frame, no outer presentation headings.
The main conversation is Shared conversations in project Dispatch Web. There are currently 3 participants: Chris, Developer, Designer. Keep a few short left-aligned messages in the main column; for example Chris: “Let's get another perspective.” Developer with Agent badge: “Reviewer would be useful here.” No agent named Reviewer is a current member yet.
Replace the right Thread panel with a Participants panel. Header Participants and close X. At top an Add participants action. Under it three participant rows: Chris — You; Developer — Agent · Following; Designer — Agent · Following. Below, selected Developer details are visible: Developer, This conversation's instance, Based on Developer, Model GPT-6 Astra. Use avatar icons only: Chris is a navy C circle, Developer a code-brackets icon, Designer a palette icon. No photographic faces.
Open a centered white modal, light dimming scrim, about 540px wide, heading Add participants with close X. Two tabs Agents (selected) and People. Search field Find an agent. Four well-spaced rows with avatars, descriptions and controls:
Reviewer — Review and critique — navy checked checkbox.
Dispatch — General assistance — empty checkbox.
Developer — Code and implementation — muted Already here label.
Designer — Product and interface design — muted Already here label.
Reviewer avatar is a magnifying glass, Dispatch robot, Developer code brackets, Designer palette; use pale aqua circles and navy line art. Existing members are clearly disabled and cannot be selected again in this invitation state.
Below list, a restrained info line reads verbatim: “New participants can read the full conversation history.” In persistent footer: 1 selected, Cancel, navy Add participant button. Keep the dialog focused; no email field, new-agent-definition form, permission roles, private-context checkbox, or automatic invitation to humans. People tab is visible to human users. Model selection is not part of invitation.
The conversation example and selected agent definitions are illustrative. Preserve the established Dispatch shell and show an understandable membership action with excellent spacing, contrast, hierarchy and exact labels.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high fidelity responsive design board of THREE tall 390px-width phone screens side by side, with narrow neutral gutters and small captions outside each screen: Conversation, Participants, Start conversation. No physical device bezels or perspective. Image 1 is the user's Slack screenshot as a structural reference ONLY: all authors left aligned in dense readable message rows, no bubbles. Do not copy its real names/content, dark theme, menu bar or Slack branding. Image 2 is the approved Dispatch workspace as the brand reference: light background, navy #1D3D6A, aqua #4DD5CF accents, Inter, thin gray-blue borders, quiet line icons. Overall landscape design board at high resolution; each phone screen approximately 390×844 CSS px with text no smaller than 12px and touch targets visually around 44px. Show consistent mobile browser app screens without browser chrome.
SCREEN 1 Conversation: compact header with small project Dispatch Web and bold Shared conversations, a labeled 4 participants button. ALL messages left aligned with 28px avatars, author+time, clear Agent badges: Chris says “Let's make this feel like a shared workspace.” Designer says “A channel-style layout gives everyone equal footing.” Under it a link 2 replies. Developer says “I'll bring Reviewer in.” Small system event Developer added Reviewer. Reviewer says “I've read the history. @Developer, keep the participant list one click away.” Plenty of readability and no background bubbles. Bottom-pinned compact Markdown composer says Message everyone… with visible @ and Send. App navigation bottom row Menu and Details with icons.
SCREEN 2 Participants: full-height mobile panel with back arrow, Participants heading and close X. Four readable rows: Chris — You; Developer — Agent · Following; Designer — Agent · Following; Reviewer — Agent · Following. An Add participant button is prominently available. Below a subtle selected-Developer detail section: Developer, “This conversation's instance”, “Based on Developer”, “GPT-6 Astra”. The panel makes reusable definitions versus current participation understandable without IDs or runtime terminology. Do not show private memory. Lower informational line: “New participants can read the full conversation history.”
SCREEN 3 Start conversation: full-screen form, back arrow and New conversation title. Small Project: Dispatch Web context. Text “Choose agents to start with.” Search field Find an agent. Four checkbox rows Dispatch — General assistance (unchecked), Developer — Code and implementation (checked), Designer — Product and interface design (checked), Reviewer — Review and critique (unchecked). Selected rows lightly aqua. A persistent bottom action area says 2 agents selected and has a full-width navy Start conversation button; Cancel is a quiet secondary action. No name or model field, no email invitation.
Keep all screens fully visible, no clipped footer. Do not add speculative product features, notifications, reactions, calls, progress graphs, private thoughts or explanatory annotations inside the product. This is a visual proposal with illustrative agents and content, not a claim of implemented screens.
